home.h1: Track your shifts, hours and pay.
home.lede: Clock in, log every job, and see an estimate of what you’ll take home.
home.heroAlt: Graft home screen showing hours worked and estimated take-home pay for the week.
home.clockP: One tap for today’s shift. Breaks pause the timer. Overnight shifts are included, and you can correct the times before you save.
home.recordsP: Look at a week, a month or a pay cycle. More than one job can sit in the same view.
home.payP: Gross, then the tax and other deductions you set on each job. In the UK and the Isle of Man that can be an illustrative PAYE or ITIP figure. Anywhere else you type your own percentages. These are estimates, not a payslip.
home.jobsP: Each job has its own rate, overtime, holiday pay and pay cycle. Save a shift as a template. Free includes 2 active jobs and 1 template.
home.remindP: A reminder before a shift, and an optional nudge when you arrive at a saved workplace. The Home Screen widget shows what’s next. A Live Activity stays up while you are clocked in.
home.backupP: Jobs, shifts and pay stay on the iPhone. Export a backup file or a CSV, or turn on an optional copy in your own iCloud.
cap.clockAlt: Graft clock screen with a shift timer running.
cap.payAlt: Graft pay screen with an estimated take-home for a pay period.
cap.recordsAlt: Graft records screen listing shifts for the period.
price.year: or yearly, with 1 month free for a new subscriber. The App Store shows the price in your country. When yearly costs less than twelve months, the subscribe screen shows how much you save.
price.fine: Monthly has no free trial. The yearly free month converts to the yearly price unless you cancel at least 24 hours before it ends. Apple bills the subscription. Prices on the subscribe button come from the App Store. Pay figures in the app are estimates, not a payslip.
sub.whereP: Open Graft, sign in, then go to Settings → Account. Monthly has no free trial. Yearly is one month free for a new subscriber, then the yearly price. The plan you pick shows the price from the App Store, with Subscribe and Restore purchases.
sub.restoreP: On the same iPhone Apple ID that bought Premium, open Settings → Account → Restore purchases. Restoring puts Premium on the Graft account you are signed in to.
sub.cancelP: Graft cannot cancel an Apple subscription from inside the app. Apple bills it and Apple cancels it.
sub.step1: Open the Settings app → your name → Subscriptions, or visit apps.apple.com/account/subscriptions.
sub.step2: Choose Graft Premium and cancel. You can also open Settings → Account → Manage subscription in Graft while Premium is active.
sub.after: The yearly free month converts to the yearly price unless you cancel at least 24 hours before the trial ends. After that, and for monthly, cancel at least 24 hours before the period ends to stop the next renewal. Premium stays available until the time you already have ends. Deleting the app, or deleting your Graft account, does not cancel the subscription.
sub.apple: Payment, renewals and refunds are handled by Apple under the Apple Licensed Application End User License Agreement.
faq.q1: Why might the pay estimate differ from my payslip?
faq.a1: Graft's figures are estimates, not a payslip. It does not know your tax code, student loan, or every deduction your employer applies. Compare the estimate with your payslip. The payslip is the source of truth.
faq.a2: Jobs, shifts and pay stay on the iPhone. Sign-in (name and email) is handled by Clerk. An iCloud backup, if you turn it on, goes to your own iCloud account. See the Privacy Policy.
faq.a3: Cancel in your App Store account settings, at least 24 hours before a trial or paid period ends. The steps are in Subscriptions. Deleting Graft does not cancel the subscription.
support.p1: Email GraftSupport@proton.me. Include the iOS version and what you expected to happen.
support.p2: Privacy questions can use the same address. The Privacy Policy and Terms of Use describe what the app does today.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.lede: Effective 8 October 2026. This page describes what the iOS app does with data today.
privacy.prevail: If a translation of this page conflicts with the English version, the English version prevails.
privacy.whoP: Email GraftSupport@proton.me. Graft does not run its own server for your shifts or pay.
privacy.account1: App Store and TestFlight builds sign you in with Clerk. Clerk stores your name, email address, and either your password (Graft never sees it) or the link to the Google or Apple account you used. Clerk also keeps the session records it needs to sign you in.
privacy.account2: Jobs, shifts, pay rates and payslip comparisons are not sent to Clerk. Settings → Account → Delete account deletes the Clerk account and the data on that device, and the iCloud copy if you had backup on.
privacy.account3: The web app, and mobile builds that are not store builds, can use an account that exists only on that device. Those passwords are stored as a salted hash, not in plaintext.
privacy.phoneLede: Unless you turn on iCloud backup, the following stays on the device:
privacy.li1: Jobs: workplace, role, colour, hourly rate, overtime, holiday pay, pay cycle, pension and the tax settings you enter.
privacy.li2: Shifts: dates, times, breaks and whether a shift is worked or scheduled.
privacy.li3: A workplace pin, if you set one. Graft keeps no location history.
privacy.li4: Preferences, including reminders, the currency used to show pay, and whether Premium is active on this account.
privacy.icloudP: Backup is off until you turn it on under Settings → Backup, privacy & data. When it is on, one copy of your Graft data (jobs, shifts, templates, clock, preferences and payslip comparisons, including a workplace pin) is saved with Apple’s iCloud key-value storage under your Apple ID. Graft cannot read that copy. Turning backup off stops saving. Deleting the account removes the copy.
privacy.subsP: Apple processes Premium payments. Graft reads the subscription status on the device. Graft does not receive your card number or Apple ID payment details.
privacy.loc1: “When in use” location lets you pin a workplace. “Always” is requested only if you turn on the arrival reminder. Graft never clocks you in by itself and does not keep a trail of where you have been.
privacy.loc2: If you search for a workplace, the text you type is sent to Photon (photon.komoot.io) and, if needed, OpenStreetMap Nominatim, to find matching places. If location permission is already granted, the search also sends a latitude and longitude so results are near you. The search does not include your Graft account, name or email. The request identifies itself as Graft.
privacy.noti: Notifications are scheduled on the phone. Graft does not register a remote push token.
privacy.cal: Calendar sync writes the job name, times and workplace into the calendar you pick. It does not write your pay.
privacy.upd: Update checks may contact Expo at u.expo.dev with the platform, runtime version, release channel and update id. That check does not include your name, email, shifts or pay.
privacy.crash: Crashes: the copy Graft keeps is on the device and is not sent to Graft. TestFlight may send crash logs to Apple under Apple’s own policy.
privacy.noads: There is no advertising and no analytics SDK. The Analytics screen calculates figures on the phone from your shifts.
privacy.rights1: Which privacy law applies depends on where you live. This is not a UK-only policy. If the UK GDPR applies to you, it applies. If another law applies — for example Thailand’s Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) — that law applies to the name and email used to sign in. Graft does not publish a postal address on this page.
privacy.rights2: Shifts and pay stay on the iPhone (and in your own iCloud only if you turn backup on). To ask about the name and email, email GraftSupport@proton.me or delete the account in the app.
privacy.childrenP: Graft is not directed at children. It is a tool for people tracking paid work.
privacy.keep1: Data on the device is removed when you delete the account or the app. An iCloud backup remains until you delete the account or turn backup off and the copy expires with Apple. Clerk’s retention of sign-in records after deletion follows Clerk’s own terms.
privacy.keep2: To ask about the name and email held for your account, email GraftSupport@proton.me or delete the account in the app.
terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.prevail: If a translation of this page conflicts with the English version, the English version prevails.
terms.licenceP: Graft is a personal tool for recording hourly shifts and estimating take-home pay. These terms cover how Graft’s subscriptions and support work. Your use of the iOS app is also licensed by Apple under the Licensed Application End User License Agreement (Apple’s standard EULA). If these terms and Apple’s EULA differ on a point Apple’s terms cover, Apple’s EULA applies to that point.
terms.estimateP: Pay figures are estimates for your own planning. They are not a payslip, not payroll, and not tax or financial advice. Graft does not apply a tax code or student loan. Illustrative UK PAYE and Isle of Man ITIP are used only when that job’s country is the UK or the Isle of Man. Everywhere else, Graft uses the percentages you enter. Your payslip is the source of truth. Do not rely on Graft for a tax or legal decision.
terms.dataP: Jobs, shifts and pay are stored on your device. Store builds sign in with Clerk, which holds your name and email, not your rota. iCloud backup is optional and off by default; the copy sits in your own iCloud account. The Privacy Policy has the detail. You can export a backup or a CSV from Settings.
terms.premiumLede: Premium is optional. On the App Store it is an auto-renewable subscription sold by Apple:
terms.month: Monthly — the monthly price shown by the App Store in your country (uk.graft.app.premium.monthly). No free trial.
terms.year: Yearly — the yearly price shown by the App Store in your country (uk.graft.app.premium.yearly). New subscribers get one month free, then that yearly price. The introductory offer is one per person for this subscription group. If yearly costs less than twelve monthly payments, the app shows the saving from the prices Apple returned.
terms.bill: Payment is charged to your Apple ID at confirmation of purchase, at the price the App Store shows. The yearly free month converts to the yearly price unless you cancel at least 24 hours before the trial ends. The subscription then renews automatically unless you cancel at least 24 hours before the end of the current period. Your account is charged for renewal within 24 hours before the end of the period. You can manage or cancel in your App Store account settings after purchase. Any unused portion of a free trial is forfeited when you buy a subscription that replaces it.
terms.where: Subscribe and restore from Settings → Account in the app. Cancelling is done by Apple, not by deleting Graft. How to cancel and restore is on the support page.
terms.flag: Outside the App Store (the web app, and non-store builds), the Premium switch is a local feature flag with no payment.
terms.useP: Use Graft for your own lawful record of work. Don’t try to break the app or use it to misuse someone else’s account.
terms.availP: Graft is provided as available. Features can change. Estimates can be wrong. To the extent the law allows, the provider is not liable for decisions you make from those estimates, or for data that was only on a device you reset. Nothing in these terms limits liability that cannot legally be limited.
terms.lawP: These terms are governed by the laws of England and Wales. If consumer law or a privacy law where you live gives you rights that cannot be waived, those rights still apply. This page does not give a postal address.
